The opponent X just dropped a piece at D4 on the bottom layer (L1). The center or near-center columns are usually strong controlling positions in Connect Four variants. Let's take control of the center by dropping our first piece at C2.

MOVE: drop C2

To continue building your strategy and contesting the center while responding to X's opening drop at A4, we want to place an O piece in a strong position. Playing `drop B2` places an O piece adjacent to your existing one at C2 on layer L1, setting up potential horizontal or diagonal lines.

MOVE: drop B2

To contest the center and block X's potential alignments while building toward your own winning lines, establishing presence in the middle columns on the bottom layer is a strong choice.

MOVE: drop C1

fts!
Let's re-read the definitions:
- "A shaft is a vertical stack of 4 cells, named like B3." This means shaft B3 consists of (Col B, Row 3, L1-L4).
So A1 is the shaft at column A, row 1. Since X just dropped into A1, A1 now has an X at L1.
Let's block X's potential threats or set up our own. O has pieces at B2, C2, C1 on L1.
O can drop into C1 to stack on C1, or drop into C3, etc.
Let's look at a defensive or constructive move. Dropping into C1 puts an O on top of the existing O at C1 (since C1 already has an O at L1, dropping into C1 will put O at L2 in shaft C1).

Let's play:
MOVE: drop C1
